clue.text: Finish at the front, in plaster?

definitions.text: Finish at the front, in plaster?

parts.words: Finish at the front, in plaster?
parts.note: the outside wall of a house can be rendered with mortar into which small stones are thrown, a rough coating finishing the frontage

explanation.surface: A question about how a plasterer completes the front of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a British exterior wall render studded with small stones, commonly on house fronts.

clue.text: Flat of the English archdeacon

parts.note: an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven

explanation.surface: Asking whether a church official's apartment is the English archdeacon's.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Church of England an archdeacon carries the title 'the Venerable', shortened to Ven.
explanation.definitionFit: Level and smooth surfaces are flat, a synonym.

clue.text: Heavy rock uniting graduate and sailor

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
an old salt is a veteran sailor

explanation.surface: A heavy-metal band formed by a university graduate and a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: A dense dark volcanic stone, a kind of rock.

clue.text: Earth design is controversial

parts.note: a design, in the sense of purpose or intention, is a motive

explanation.surface: A planet-themed design is said to be causing an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arousing strong feelings tends to be divisive and disputed.

clue.text: Voice heard in loyal toast

indicators.note: the letters are to be found running across the words of the toast that follow

explanation.surface: A voice ringing out as a patriotic toast is drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard in' marks the hidden run across 'loyAL TOast'; it does not signal a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: A singing part, the lower female or high male register, is a voice.

clue.text: This jet arrived in yesterday from Paris

indicators.note: the abbreviation for arrived is placed inside the French word

parts.note: hier is the French word for yesterday
arr. is the timetable abbreviation for arrived

explanation.surface: A jet aircraft that landed yesterday after a flight from Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A British vertical take-off fighter plane, a jet aircraft.

clue.text: So much wine upset Hamlet's hue

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so these letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: Drinking too much has drained the colour from Hamlet's face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges HAMLETSHUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A very large wine bottle, holding eight standard bottles, is named after a biblical patriarch.

clue.text: Chaps to go abroad with wild beasts at noon

definitions.text: Chaps to go abroad with wild beasts at noon

parts.words: Chaps to go abroad with wild beasts at noon
parts.note: recalls the Noel Coward song about mad dogs and these men, who alone go out in the midday sun

explanation.surface: Men venturing overseas alongside crazed animals in the heat of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel Coward's song says only 'mad dogs and ...' go out in the midday sun; the wild beasts are the mad dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Males from a particular country are its chaps, here the nation of the song.

clue.text: Light none put out

indicators.note: put out suggests disturbed or disarranged, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A light that nobody switched off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges NONE; it looks like extinguishing a light.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas used in glowing advertising tubes, so a kind of light.

clue.text: Toy to make the pulse race?

definitions.text: Toy to make the pulse race?

parts.words: Toy to make the pulse race?
parts.note: pulses are dried seeds such as peas, and a child's tube blows them out at speed

explanation.surface: A thrilling toy that sets the heart pounding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' means legumes, not heartbeat: this toy sends small round seeds racing through the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's blowpipe for firing dried seeds, a plaything.

clue.text: Girl with pain in both sides

indicators.note: the pain sits between the two side letters

parts.note: both sides are right and left, R and L
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: A girl suffering pain down both sides of her body.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, so it can stand for a girl.

clue.text: Back-slapping-when loud-is French, I have concluded

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical direction for loud
est is the French for is
contracted, I have becomes I've

explanation.surface: A jovial Frenchman, noisy and pleased with himself, declares the matter settled.
explanation.definitionFit: Jolly and celebratory, as at a party full of hearty congratulation.

clue.text: The flight out that leads to safety

definitions.text: The flight out that leads to safety

parts.words: The flight out that leads to safety
parts.note: a flight here is a set of stairs, used for getting out of a burning building

explanation.surface: An aeroplane departure that carries refugees to safety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests a plane but means a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: An external staircase for leaving a building in a blaze, a way out to safety.

clue.text: Girl has mean quality and unhealthy complexion

parts.note: Sal is a short girl's name
lowness is the quality of being base or mean

explanation.surface: A girl with a mean streak and a sickly skin tone.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellowish pallid skin is a sign of poor health in the face.

clue.text: Bar for unorthodox poets

indicators.note: unorthodox means unconventional, so the letters are set in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A pub frequented by unconventional poets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unorthodox' rearranges POETS.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal term meaning to preclude or prevent, i.e. to bar.

clue.text: Fabulous horse whose feet hardly touched the ground!

definitions.text: Fabulous horse whose feet hardly touched the ground!

parts.words: Fabulous horse whose feet hardly touched the ground!
parts.note: describes a mythical winged steed that flew, so its hooves barely met the earth

explanation.surface: A racehorse so fast it seemed to fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means from fable, not wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged horse of Greek myth is a creature of fable that flies.

clue.text: Safe temperature, equal all round

indicators.note: the equal goes all round the abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: a peer is an equal

explanation.surface: A thermostat setting giving a safe, even temperature everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Old criminal slang for a strongbox or safe that thieves crack.

clue.text: Variety of trees in compound

indicators.note: a variety is a different arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Different sorts of trees growing in an enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety of' rearranges TREES; 'compound' is chemical, not an enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: An organic chemical compound formed from an acid and an alcohol.

clue.text: Record spin

definitions.meaning: a register or list of names, as in a class register
to turn over and over, as dice or a ball does

explanation.surface: Putting a record on the turntable to spin.
explanation.definitionFit: A roster is an official list or record; to rotate or tumble is to turn over.

clue.text: Prize for Victoria, say

definitions.meaning: a choice job or reward, the best one going
Victoria is a well-known variety of this fruit

explanation.surface: An award going to someone called Victoria.
explanation.walkthrough: A Victoria is a common British variety of the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A plum job is a prize one; Victoria is a variety of the stone fruit.

clue.text: Fought and then made ready for presentation

definitions.meaning: engaged in a fist fight in the ring
packed in a case ready to be given as a gift

explanation.surface: A boxer won a fight and then was groomed for an award.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparred in the ring; and packed in a carton for giving.

clue.text: Retriever, for example, casts shadow on prison

indicators.note: in a down entry the shadow piece is placed after the prison piece

parts.note: bird is slang for a prison sentence, from rhyming slang bird-lime for time
to dog someone is to follow or shadow them

explanation.surface: A dog's shadow falls across a jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing bird' is British slang for serving time in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun dog trained to fetch shot game, of which a retriever is one kind.

clue.text: Trap villain by Barrow, say

indicators.note: the cart piece stands beside the villain piece

parts.note: a dog is a contemptible scoundrel, a villain
a barrow is an example of a cart

explanation.surface: A villain springing a trap near the town of Barrow.
explanation.walkthrough: A trap is a light two-wheeled horse carriage; Barrow is also a town in Cumbria.
explanation.definitionFit: A small horse-drawn carriage, originally with a box for dogs, is a kind of trap.

clue.text: Pleasant experience for number one?

parts.note: number one means oneself, and an indulgent outing flatters the self

explanation.surface: A treat for the person at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number one' is oneself; the experience gratifies one's own vanity.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-indulgent act done to boost one's own sense of importance.

clue.text: To make crude gun, hero improvised

indicators.note: improvised means put together on the spot, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hero hastily cobbles together a crude gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improvised' rearranges GUN and HERO.
explanation.definitionFit: To coarsen or make less smooth is to make crude.

clue.text: Boyish girl, sort of enigma

indicators.note: to sort is to rearrange, so these letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: A tomboyish girl who is something of a mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges ENIGMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A slim girl with an elfin, boyish charm.

clue.text: The French duck a false report

definitions.meaning: the French word for a duck
a baseless rumour or hoax story

explanation.surface: A French duck becomes the subject of a hoax news story.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for a duck; and a hoax or unfounded rumour.

clue.text: Twin, as found in a thesaurus?

indicators.note: the letters are found lying inside the single word that follows

explanation.surface: Looking up a twin's name in a book of synonyms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' shows the run inside 'thESAUrus'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob's brother in Genesis, born first of a pair of twins.

clue.text: Navy in the doldrums?

definitions.meaning: navy is a dark shade of this colour

explanation.surface: A sailor stuck in becalmed waters.
explanation.walkthrough: The doldrums are a windless ocean zone and also low spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Navy is a dark shade of the colour; to be sad is to be in low spirits.

clue.text: Stunning person liable to change into something more comfortable?

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive, stunning person

indicators.note: to change means to alter, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An attractive person likely to slip into something more comfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges LIABLE into ABILLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of being casually or partly dressed, in loose informal clothes.

clue.text: Infatuation with soft wood

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for soft
ash is a kind of tree and its wood

explanation.surface: Falling for a gentle woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a schoolgirl crush, a passionate fondness.

clue.text: Dressed to participate in the hit-parade?

definitions.text: Dressed to participate in the hit-parade?

parts.words: Dressed to participate in the hit-parade?
parts.note: running the gauntlet means passing between rows of men striking you, so a hit-parade; the word also means wearing armoured gloves

explanation.surface: Kitted out to appear in the pop music charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit-parade' is not the charts but a line of people dealing blows, as in running the gauntlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing heavy protective gloves, i.e. dressed in them.
